confirmed.claim: checkpointed() parses every sidecar line with read_jsonl and has no tolerance for a partial trailing row, and because run() now wraps load_document/completed/ingest in one try, the JSONDecodeError is swallowed as a per-document ERROR on every run: a document whose sidecar (or, via completed() at line 1141, whose package) was cut short by a hard kill is never ingested again until someone deletes the file by hand.
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced offline: a sidecar for graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.txt holding one good unit row plus a row truncated at half its length (what a SIGKILL, OOM kill or Kaggle session-limit kill leaves when it lands inside one of the ~1,177 per-unit appends of a 10-200 KB row at line 1185-1186) makes run([uri]) log 'ERROR JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string ...', make zero calls, write no package and leave the sidecar in place; a second run does exactly the same (done 0, skipped 0). On Kaggle the file is seeded into every later version by seed_from_prior_output, so the document silently drops out of the corpus with one ERROR line among 329, and nothing in the receipt distinguishes it from a bad document. Before the patch no on-disk state could poison a document, and a corrupt package aborted the run visibly instead of being skipped.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by reproduction against the current file (scratch script exec'ing the notebook blocks with the battery's scripted generate, OUT pointed at a temp dir). checkpointed() at line 1160 reads the sidecar through read_jsonl() (line 89, bare json.loads per line, no guard), and run() at lines 1341-1362 now wraps load_document/completed/ingest in one try whose `except Exception` logs 'ERROR' and continues. Steps: ingest oz/01_55.txt with a scripted stop after 3 units (sidecar: 3 rows, 66,505 bytes, ~22 KB per row, so a kill inside one of the per-unit appends at lines 1273-1275 leaving a partial line is realistic); cut the last row at half its length; run([uri]) -> 'ERROR JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 14806', 0 calls, no package, sidecar left in place (the unlink at line 1267 is never reached because checkpointed raised first); run([uri]) again -> identical result, done 0 skipped 0. The document is never ingested again until the sidecar is deleted by hand, and on Kaggle seed_from_prior_output (lines 64-84) copies the *.units.jsonl into every later version, so the poison persists across versions. The same holds for a package truncated mid write_text (line 1130): completed() at line 1141 raises inside the try, the document is reported as ERROR and skipped every run; additionally receipt() at line 1379 raises JSONDecodeError on that package and produces no receipt.json at all (reproduced: 'receipt raised JSONDecodeError Expecting ':' delimiter'). The old file (1cbc36d) had no sidecar and called completed() outside the try, so a corrupt package aborted visibly rather than being skipped silently. No money is wasted and the run continues, so major rather than blocker: one document per hard kill is silently lost from the corpus with only an ERROR line to show for it.
confirmed.fix: Add a forgiving reader for the ingestor's own files and use it in checkpointed(), completed() and receipt(): def read_jsonl_prefix(path): rows = []; for line in path.open(encoding='utf-8'): if line.strip(): try: rows.append(json.loads(line)) except json.JSONDecodeError: break; return rows. In checkpointed() (line 1160) build `rows` from read_jsonl_prefix(side), also guard the row shape (`isinstance(r.get('rec'), dict) and 'unit_id' in r['rec']`), and after computing `kept`, if len(kept) < number of parsed lines or a decode error was hit, rewrite the sidecar with just the kept rows before ingest() appends to it (or simply unlink it when kept is empty; ingest already does that at line 1267 when records is empty, which is reached once checkpointed no longer raises). In completed() (line 1136) and receipt() (line 1379) read with the same helper so a truncated package yields no completion record: completed() returns None and write_package overwrites it; receipt() skips it instead of crashing. Optionally note('... sidecar/package truncated, resuming from N units') so the operator sees it in ingest.log.

confirmed.claim: fold() asks the model for at most max(10, limit*9//10) words but enforces `word_count(text) > limit` with limit = child_words // 2, so whenever the children hold fewer than 20 words the prompt's number exceeds the enforced bound and a reply that obeys the prompt is rejected, retried with a contradicting limit, and usually left unstamped.
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced by calling fold() with children ['is_a girl', 'lives_in Kansas', 'has_trait brave', '[c1] Dorothy acts in the unit today.'] (13 words, three-plus children so the len(children) <= 2 shortcut at line 989 does not apply): limit 6, prompt says 'at most 10 words', a 10-word reply is rejected twice, result (None, ['(over length)'], 6). A document-major with two or three short facts and one one-sentence cell is common for secondary characters, so each such entity costs two Luna entity_abstract calls and ends in entity_abstract_rejected with no abstract.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by reading and by reproduction. In the current file, fold() (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py lines 911-913) sets limit = min(400, max(1, child_words // 2)) but sends the prompt max(10, limit * 9 // 10), so for every children set under 20 words (limit 1..9) the prompt names a number larger than the bound line 921 enforces (`word_count(text) > limit`). Exec-ing the notebook blocks the way the battery does with a stub that returns exactly the words the prompt asks for: children ['is_a girl', 'lives_in Kansas', 'has_trait brave', '[c1] Dorothy acts in the unit today.'] (13 words) give limit 6, both attempts are asked for "at most 10 words", and fold returns (None, ['(over length)'], 6) after two entity_abstract calls. With a stub that reads the retry's "against a limit of 6" clause and obeys it, the second call is accepted, so on the real model the usual cost is one wasted Luna call per such entity (the base prompt still says 10; only the appended sentence says 6), and an entity is left in entity_abstract_rejected whenever the retry also lands at 7-10 words or the limit is too small to write a sentence in (child_words 6-7 gives limit 3). Only per-entity abstracts are affected: the document fold's children are unit summaries, whose total is always over 20 words, and the len(children) <= 2 shortcut at line 989 covers the 1-2 child case, so the exposure is document-majors with three or more short fact/cell children, which is plausible for secondary characters. The battery never exercises it because its scripted fold reply is always a few words. Severity minor: bounded extra spend and some missing entity abstracts, no wrong records.
confirmed.fix: Line 913: never ask for more than the bound, e.g. `prompt = fold_prompt(what, children, limit if limit < 12 else limit * 9 // 10)`; or extend the line-989 shortcut so children totalling under 20 words stand as the abstract without a fold call.

confirmed.claim: For a document resumed from its sidecar, stats['calls'] and stats['cost'] (and therefore the completion record, the manifest row and receipt.cost_of_packages) count only the resuming session's calls; the derive calls paid in the earlier session are in that session's calls.jsonl, which seed_from_prior_output deliberately does not copy, so the per-document cost the brief's acceptance list asks for is lost for every document that crossed a stop.
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced offline: graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.txt stopped at the fold after all 10 units were derived ($0.030 in the stub's costs); the resumed run finished it with two calls and wrote completion stats {'calls': 2, 'cost': 0.002} and a manifest row with cost 0.002, and receipt.cost_of_packages summed the 0.002. On Kaggle the $0.5-1.0 of Luna spend on a large Greek or Holmes document that crossed the $25 stop is attributed to no package, and the 'within 20 percent of the demo's cost' comparison for a resumed Oz book reads far too low.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by reading and by reproduction. In ingest() (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py line 1257) before_calls/before_spend are taken from CALLS at the start of the resuming session, and line 1287 sets stats['calls'] and stats['cost'] from that delta; the sidecar rows written at line 1271 carry only {ingestor, input_hash, rec} with no cost, and seed_from_prior_output (line 76) skips the prior session's calls.jsonl on purpose. So for a document that crossed a stop, the completion record's stats, the manifest row (line 1344) and receipt.cost_of_packages (line 1387) count only the resuming session's calls. Scratch run with the battery's stub on graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.txt: stop after 11 calls ($0.011), clear CALLS to simulate a new Kaggle session, resume: completion stats {'calls': 25, 'cost': 0.025}, manifest cost 0.025, receipt cost_of_packages 0.025, true total 36 calls / $0.036. The finding's line 1192 is wrong (that is show_unit); the defect is at line 1287 with its baseline at 1257. Severity stays minor: nothing is mis-derived and no money is wasted; only the one document in flight at each stop is under-counted, the per-session totals in the receipt remain correct, and the missing amount is still recoverable from the earlier version's calls.jsonl. It does break the brief's 'cost per document' acceptance item (ingestor-brief.md line 155) for exactly those documents, and would misread the Oz comparison only if Oz book 1 itself crossed the stop.
confirmed.fix: Carry the cost in the sidecar. At line 1271 write each row with the unit's own spend: {"ingestor": INGESTOR, "input_hash": ..., "calls": len(CALLS) - calls_at, "cost": round(spend() - at, 4), "rec": rec} (take calls_at = len(CALLS) next to `at = spend()` on line 1268). Have checkpointed() return the kept rows rather than bare recs (or return a second value summing row.get("calls", 0) and row.get("cost", 0.0) over the kept rows; .get keeps old sidecars valid), and in ingest() add those sums at line 1287: "calls": len(CALLS) - before_calls + prior_calls, "cost": round(spend() - before_spend + prior_cost, 4). The battery's resume check (test_ingestor.py line 303) should then also assert rows[-1]["stats"]["calls"] == 3 units' worth plus the resumed calls.

confirmed.claim: When completed(doc) skips a document, a sidecar for it that was seeded from an older version's output (a version that stopped inside the document before a later version finished it) is left in place, so receipt.in_flight_sidecars reports it as in flight and every later version copies it forward again.
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced offline: a completed package for graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.txt plus a stale Novel-40700.units.jsonl beside it; run([uri]) reports skipped 1, the sidecar remains, and receipt() lists 'graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.units.jsonl' under in_flight_sidecars while documents is 1. On Kaggle this happens whenever two previous versions' outputs are attached at once (the stopped one and the one that finished), which the header's 'attach that version's output' instruction does not warn against.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by reading and by an offline reproduction. In run() (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py line 1336) `if completed(doc): skipped += 1; continue` returns before ingest() is called, and the only sidecar unlinks are inside ingest() (line 1266 when the sidecar holds nothing usable, line 1295 after write_package). seed_from_prior_output (lines 64-83) copies every non-log *.jsonl under any attached 'packages' folder, sidecars included, whenever OUT lacks it, with no check for a finished package of the same stem; Kaggle keeps attached inputs across Save & Run All unless removed, so a stopped version and the version that finished the document being attached together is the ordinary case. Scratch script (notebook blocks exec'd with the battery's scripted model): run graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.txt to completion (sidecar gone), write a one-unit sidecar with the current INGESTOR and matching input_hash beside the package, run again: done 0 skipped 1, sidecar still present, receipt() gives documents 1 and in_flight_sidecars ['graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.units.jsonl']. No money is spent and no package record is wrong; checkpointed()'s version/hash filter keeps the stale sidecar from ever being replayed. The cost is a stray file carried forward every version and a false in-flight line in the receipt. The finding's line 1237 is show_fold in the current file; the correct anchor is line 1336.
confirmed.fix:
In run(), at line 1336, remove a leftover sidecar when a document is skipped as complete:

            if completed(doc):
                side = sidecar_path(doc)
                if side.exists():
                    side.unlink()
                skipped += 1
                continue

Optionally also harden seed_from_prior_output: after copying, skip (or delete) any `*.units.jsonl` whose sibling package `path.with_suffix('').with_suffix('.jsonl')` exists in OUT, so a stale sidecar from an older attached version is never carried forward.

confirmed.claim: The run has no wall-clock stop, and the sample cannot finish sequentially inside Kaggle's 12-hour limit; a timed-out Save & Run All is a failed version whose /kaggle/working is discarded, so every package and calls.jsonl are lost while every call was billed.
confirmed.scenario: RUN='sample' is 329 documents, 1,177 units, 10.0M characters (measured: 600 chat units at 7.3k chars, 293 paper units at 5.7k, 284 book units at 7.7k-14.3k). Derive alone is ~2,900 Luna calls (300 chat header units stop after the entity call), plus ~300 embeds, ~1,200 entity-abstract folds, and Terra judge batches on the nine books; roughly 4,500 sequential HTTPS calls. At 10 s a call that is 12.5 h; at a realistic 15-20 s for a 3-4k-token unit producing a facts list it is 19-25 h. SPEND_STOP=25 will not bind first (projected spend is about $8-10 at the PRICE table), so the only thing that ends the run is Kaggle killing it, and a killed commit keeps no output. Result: all the money spent, no packages, no calls.jsonl to resume from.
confirmed.what_happens: Partly stale premise, but the defect stands. What is wrong in the finding: the current file does not run the sample at $25 on Kaggle. Block 12 (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py lines 1434-1438, and the same in the generated .ipynb) sets RUN = ["/oz/01_55.txt"] and forces SPEND_STOP = 5.00 when /kaggle/working exists (commit d745d67 after a57911b changed a57911b's `SPEND_STOP = 25.00`), so the imminent Save & Run All is Oz book 1 alone: 24 units, and the 09-02 demo of the same three Luna calls per chapter plus Terra judge ran the whole book in 35 min (cell timestamps in log/2026-09-02/it494-chapter-ingestion-oz-book-1.ipynb: 13:33:00 to 14:08:41; 69 Luna derive calls in 897.8 s = 13.0 s per call; ~113 judge calls in 795 s). No 12 h risk for that run. What is right: call() at lines 216-221 checks only spend(); nothing in the file reads the wall clock, and run() has no other exit. The sample measured from the real export (scratch exec of blocks 1 and 11) is 329 documents, 1,177 units, 8.9M chars (600 chat units at 7.3k chars, 293 paper units at 5.7k, 284 book units at 7.7k-14.3k). Derive alone is ~2,930 sequential Luna calls (300 headers stop after the entity call, 877 units x 3), which at the measured 13 s is 10.6 h before any judge batch, fold, entity-abstract or embed call, so the full sample cannot finish in one 12 h version at any SPEND_STOP the header invites the user to set ("set RUN and SPEND_STOP in block 12"; block 12's comment: "Later runs set RUN to 'sample'"). Even at the $5 line, my cost arithmetic from the demo ($0.0025 per Luna call on a 4k-word chapter, scaled to the smaller chat and paper units, plus ~$1.2 of paper judge) puts $5 near the end of the paper phase, i.e. roughly 8.5-11 h in, so the spend stop is not guaranteed to bind before Kaggle kills the session. Kaggle community reports ("[Bug] Can't access output files after 12-hour timeout", product-feedback/532451; "Unable to download the output of 'timeout exceeded' notebook", questions-and-answers/535418) say a timed-out version's /kaggle/working is not retrievable, so packages, sidecars and calls.jsonl written during those hours are lost while every call was billed. Not a blocker because the run about to happen is unaffected and a $5 sample run probably stops first; major because the first sample version is a coin-flip on losing $5 and ~10 h of output, and RUN="all" (44,262 units) is certain to hit it unless the stop is left at $5.
confirmed.fix: Add a wall-clock stop beside the spend stop. Block 1: `START = time.time()`. Block 12, next to `SPEND_STOP = 5.00`: `WALL_STOP = float(os.environ.get("WALL_STOP", "39600"))` (11 h; unlimited locally via env). In call() right after the spend check at line 221: `elapsed = time.time() - START` / `if elapsed >= WALL_STOP: raise SpendStop(f"time stop: {elapsed / 3600:.1f} h of {WALL_STOP / 3600:.1f}")`. run() already catches SpendStop, keeps the sidecar and calls.jsonl, and the finally-block writes the receipt, so the version completes with its output saved for the next resume. Add one sentence to the header: a full sample takes two or three versions; RUN="all" many.

confirmed.claim: The header and the README tell the user to resume by attaching 'that version's output' via Add Input > Your Work, but Kaggle refuses a notebook's own output as its input (circular dependency); the mechanism only works through a dataset made from the output, which the code does handle.
confirmed.scenario: After a stopped version, the user opens Add Input > Your Work > threadatlas-ingestor and Kaggle rejects it as self-referential, so the run restarts from zero and pays for the finished documents again unless the user knows to create a dataset from the version's Output tab (which mounts as /kaggle/input/<dataset>/packages/... and is found by seed_from_prior_output's rglob('packages')).
confirmed.what_happens: The instruction at notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py lines 21-23 ("attach that version's output as an input (Add Input > Your Work)") points at a route Kaggle does not offer for the same notebook: a notebook's own output cannot be attached as its own input (Kaggle only lets a notebook's output feed a different notebook, and there is no way to attach an older version's output at all; the supported route for one's own prior output is Create Dataset from the version's Output tab, or forking). The code itself is fine: seed_from_prior_output (lines 64-83) rglobs '/kaggle/input' for any 'packages' directory and copies every non-log *.jsonl into OUT when missing, so a dataset made from the output (mounted as /kaggle/input/<slug>/packages/...) or a forked notebook's attachment both seed correctly. Consequence is friction, not silent money loss: the user follows the header, cannot find the notebook under Your Work, and has to work out the dataset step; only if they then Save & Run All with nothing attached does the run re-pay for finished documents. One part of the claim is wrong: README.md has no 'Your Work' or resume text at all, so only the notebook header needs changing. No line in the current file writes wrong records; severity minor.
confirmed.fix: In notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py lines 21-23 replace "attach that version's output as an input (Add Input > Your Work)" with "open the stopped version's Output tab, Create Dataset from it, and Add Input > Datasets > that dataset (a fork of this notebook can instead attach the original under Add Input > Your Work)". Leave seed_from_prior_output as is; it already finds either mount by the 'packages' folder. No README change is needed since README has no resume instruction.

confirmed.claim: For a document resumed from its sidecar, stats.cost and stats.calls count only this session's calls, so the completion record, the manifest row and receipt.cost_of_packages understate the document's true cost, and the prior session's calls.jsonl is deliberately not carried, so the corpus total is recoverable only by summing calls.jsonl across versions by hand.
confirmed.scenario: Version 1 derives 20 of Oz book 1's 26 units ($0.40) and stops; version 2 with the output attached derives 6 units, judges and folds ($0.15) and writes completion stats.cost=0.15. receipt.json says cost_of_packages 0.15 for that document and cost_this_session 0.15; the $0.40 appears in no receipt.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by code and by a two-namespace reproduction (fresh namespace = fresh Kaggle session with CALLS empty, same OUT). ingest() sets before_calls/before_spend at line 1256 of notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py from the in-memory CALLS, replays the sidecar records (1258-1261) which carry no cost, and at 1287 writes stats.calls/cost = this session's delta only. Reproduction on graphrag-bench/Novel-40700 (10 units): session 1 stopped after 11 calls ($0.011, 3 units checkpointed); session 2 resumed with 25 calls ($0.025). Completion stats {'calls': 25, 'cost': 0.025}, manifest row 0.025, receipt cost_of_packages 0.025 and cost_this_session 0.025, against a true document cost of $0.036 / 36 calls. seed_from_prior_output (line 76) deliberately skips the prior calls.jsonl, so the $0.011 exists only in version 1's own calls.jsonl. The finding's anchor line 1192 is in show_unit; the defect sits at 1256/1287 (stats) and 1275-1276 (sidecar row without cost). Minor: no money wasted, packages and facts correct, cost_this_session is accurate as labelled; only the per-document cost of documents resumed across sessions (the brief's 'cost per document' deliverable) is understated, and only when a run actually stops mid-document.
confirmed.fix: In ingest(): before derive_unit record `calls_at = len(CALLS)` next to `at = spend()` (line 1273) and write `"cost": round(spend() - at, 6), "calls": len(CALLS) - calls_at` into the sidecar row at line 1276. In checkpointed() (1171-1181) return the rows (or a parallel list of their cost/calls) rather than only r["rec"], and in ingest() sum the replayed rows into `prior_cost, prior_calls`, then at line 1287 use `"calls": prior_calls + len(CALLS) - before_calls, "cost": round(prior_cost + spend() - before_spend, 4)`. The receipt then sums correctly from the completion records with no change; optionally note in the receipt that calls.jsonl covers this session only.

confirmed.claim: receipt() counts any package ending in a completion record, without checking its ingestor or input_hash, so packages seeded from an older version's output (or for documents outside this RUN) are reported as this version's documents and cost.
confirmed.scenario: A 0.1 output with 329 packages is attached to a 0.2 run with RUN=['/oz/01_55.txt']; seed copies all 329 into /kaggle/working/packages, 0.2 rewrites one, and receipt.json reports documents=329, cost_of_packages summed over 0.1 stats, empty_completions and matched_by from 0.1 — figures that will be read as the 0.2 run's.
confirmed.what_happens: The code gap is real and reproduced, but the scenario as written cannot happen in the run about to start. receipt() at notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py lines 1359-1390 (current file; the finding's 1274 is the old numbering) accepts any file whose last line is record=="completion" (line 1377) and never looks at last["ingestor"] or last["input_hash"], while stamping the result "ingestor": INGESTOR (line 1361); seed_from_prior_output() at lines 64-83 copies every non-run-log *.jsonl under any /kaggle/input/**/packages with no version check. Reproduction: exec'd blocks 1-12 the way the battery does against the real export (19,436 documents), dropped one package under OUT/oz/02_54.jsonl with a 0.1-shaped completion (0.1 at 1cbc36d writes the same counts/stats keys, so nothing raises), and called receipt(): it reported ingestor "threadatlas-ingestor 0.2", documents 1, by_group {oz: 1}, cost_of_packages 1.75, matched_by/rejected_by from the stale record, while completed() for the same document correctly returned None (input_hash folds INGESTOR, line 1022). So stale-version packages are re-derived when named in RUN but, when not named, are silently reported as this version's documents and cost. Why it is only minor and not a risk to this run: no ingestor version has ever produced a Kaggle output (log/2026-09-06/README.md lists "The real run, on Kaggle" under Open; the extractor runs are the only Kaggle versions), there is no data/packages locally and none tracked, so there is nothing of 0.1 to attach or seed; the 329-package premise does not exist today. It becomes reachable at the first version bump after this run, because the header (lines 17-25) tells Justin to attach the previous version's output to continue, and audit.md row "Re-runs mint nothing" says a bump invalidates every package by design; then the receipt of a 0.3 run seeded from 0.2 output would mix the two versions under one ingestor stamp. Same-version seeding (0.2 output attached to a 0.2 run) is counted by design ("Sums over every package on disk") and is not wrong.
confirmed.fix: In receipt() (line 1377), extend the skip: `if not last or last.get("record") != "completion": continue` followed by `if last.get("ingestor") != INGESTOR: rec["stale_packages"] = rec.get("stale_packages", 0) + 1; continue` (add "stale_packages": 0 to the rec dict on line 1361). That keeps foreign-version packages on disk for the resume flow but out of this version's documents, counts, matched_by, rejected_by and cost_of_packages, and makes their presence visible. Optionally also have seed_from_prior_output() skip a package whose last record's ingestor differs, but that is not needed once the receipt filters.

confirmed.claim: A quote whose normalised form is empty (only soft hyphens, U+00AD, which QUOTES now maps to '') produces an empty pattern; re.search('', ntext) matches at 0 with m.end()==0, so back[m.end()-1] is back[-1] and locate returns the whole unit as a 'normalised' match; derive_unit (line 621) then stores the entire unit text as the fact's quote. Before the patch nothing mapped to '' so this path could not be reached.
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced with the current block 4 exec'd the way test_ingestor.py does: locate('Dorothy lived in Kansas.', '­') -> (0, 24, 'normalised'); same for two soft hyphens. Exposure is small (only 2 export documents contain U+00AD and both are mojibake bytes of an emoji, and a model would have to return a soft-hyphen-only quote), so no money and almost certainly no record, but it is a wrong-record path with a one-line guard. Everything else in the soft-hyphen handling checks out: on 'recon­ciliation of the ac­counts was done.' the quotes 'reconciliation', 'recon', 'ciliation of the accounts', 'accounts was' all locate and each slice normalises back to the quote (the end offset lands on the soft hyphen and excludes it); surface_spans('recon') is (0,5) and 'accounts' is (23,32).
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by exec'ing the current block 4 (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py, commit a57911b) the way test_ingestor.py does. U+00AD is category Cf, so `(quote or "").strip()` at line 392 does not remove it and the "empty" guard at line 393 is not taken; `normalised("­")` returns "" because QUOTES (line 361) now maps it to ""; `nwords` at line 404 is `[]`; the pattern at line 405 is the empty string, which matches at 0 with m.end()==0, and line 407 evaluates `back[-1] + 1`, i.e. the whole unit. Observed: locate("Dorothy lived in Kansas.", "­") -> (0, 24, "normalised"), same for "­­" and " ­ ". derive_unit (line 621, `quote = text[start:end]`) would then store the entire unit text as the fact's quote with matched_by "normalised" and quote_start/quote_end spanning the unit. Before the patch nothing normalised to "", so the path was unreachable. The finding's description of surface_spans is slightly off but the defect there is real and worse than stated: with the same soft-hyphen-only surface, line 434 builds `(?<!\w)(?!\w)`, which matches at zero-width positions between non-word characters; on "a. b" it returns [(2, 2)] (a zero-width mention span), and on "Dorothy lived in Kansas." it matches only at position 24 == len(ntext), so line 435 raises IndexError (back[24]). That exception is not caught in derive_unit; it propagates to run()'s `except Exception` at line 1349, which logs ERROR and skips the whole document (or re-raises with stop_on_error=True), after the entity call for that unit has already been paid for. Reachability is the mitigating factor: the model would have to return a quote or surface form consisting only of soft hyphens; only 2 export documents even contain U+00AD (mojibake), so in practice no money and almost certainly no record are at stake. Severity minor, as filed.
confirmed.fix: In locate, after line 404 (`nwords = nq.split()`), add `if not nwords: return None, None, "empty"`. In surface_spans, after line 433 (`ns, _ = normalised(s)`), add `nw = ns.split()` followed by `if not nw: return []`, and build the line-434 pattern from `nw`. Both are one-line guards; the battery's scripted model can add a case with quote "­" and surface form "­" expecting a rejected "empty" fact and no mention.

confirmed.scenario:

refuted.claim: input_hash includes INGESTOR, so any version bump (0.2 -> 0.3, even a prompt wording fix) makes completed() reject every seeded package and re-derive the whole corpus; this is intentional but said nowhere, and the header promises only that 'finished packages are copied in and skipped'.
refuted.why: The mechanics are as claimed: `input_hash()` at line 1023 of notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py hashes INGESTOR along with doc_id and unit ids, `completed()` (line 1143) and `checkpointed()` (line 1174) compare against it, so a 0.3 bump makes every seeded 0.2 package non-complete and `write_package` overwrites it (and the 0.2 sidecar is unlinked at the `if not records and side.exists()` branch). But this is not a defect in the patch: it is a recorded project decision, stated in log/2026-09-06/audit.md line 51 ("A version bump of the ingestor invalidates every package by design"), and the finding's own premise ("said nowhere") is wrong on that point. Nothing about the run that is about to happen (0.2, either fresh or resuming a 0.2 output) fails, writes wrong records, or wastes money; the scenario needs a hypothetical future 0.3 plus a deliberate choice to attach 0.2 output, and re-deriving under a changed prompt/version is the conservative behaviour for a package whose provenance record says which ingestor derived it. Splitting the hash so a "compatible" bump reuses old packages would let records stamped `ingestor: 0.3` in provenance sit next to lines actually produced by 0.2, which is worse than the current rule. The remaining substance is a one-line documentation gap in the notebook header (line 22-23 says only "finished packages are copied in and skipped"), which is style/wording, not a reportable defect under the brief.
